target: Software engineering intern roles at quantitative trading / HFT firms (Jane Street, HRT, Citadel Securities, Optiver, IMC style), 2026–27 cycle. Score domain_fit for this domain.
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28 who built a C++17 IEX order book replaying 50.9M real messages at ~687 ns/event, with real perf methodology; AWS and Capital One internships.

score_rationale.quantification: Latency is a mean only, no tail or distribution; '1.41× a passive mirror book' is a confusing baseline that makes me re-read.
score_rationale.concision_readability: Project bullets pack too many numbers per line; the batch-sizing parenthetical is four metrics stacked together and hard to parse at a glance.

must_fix: clarify: whether 686.7 ns/event is a mean only; if you have p50/p99 or other tail numbers, a tail number is what an HFT reviewer looks for first
clarify: what '1.41× a passive mirror book (485.6 ns)' means; it reads like an overhead ratio but needs a plain explanation of what the mirror book skips
clarify: 'Published' a negative result—where? If it is a README or writeup in the repo, say 'Documented' to avoid implying a publication

bullets.quote: Engineered a C++17 order book and matching engine
bullets.issue: Strong correctness claim; 'Engineered' is filler and C++17 repeats the header.
bullets.suggestion: Built an order book and matching engine that replayed 50.9M real IEX DEEP+ messages with no resync, matching 99,122 of 99,123 fills exactly and 100% of top-of-book prices

bullets.quote: Benchmarked B+ tree vs LSM skip-list stores
bullets.issue: Solid trade-off, but event-log storage is off the hot path; keep it shorter so it doesn't outrank latency work.
bullets.suggestion: Benchmarked B+ tree vs LSM skip-list event-log stores on identical 2M-record workloads: B+ tree gave 12.8× read throughput and 22× faster range summaries for 27% more disk

bullets.quote: Published an adaptive batch-sizing policy as a negative
bullets.issue: Honest and good, but the metric stack is hard to parse; the conclusion should come first.
bullets.suggestion: Documented a negative result: adaptive batch sizing gave no query win (+71% disk, −32% append rate) because cost is dominated by node lookup, not batch size

bullets.issue: Most domain-relevant bullet, but it's buried fourth, gives only a mean, and the mirror-book comparison is unclear.
bullets.suggestion: Move to second. Sustained 1.26M events/sec end-to-end; matching engine averages 686.7 ns/event at a fixed 1.40 GHz clock vs 485.6 ns for a passive mirror book with no matching

bullets.quote: Traced a 1.65× phantom regression to a CPU-governor
Writing Java policies that tune upper/lower bounds
Precomputed a tree-style search index over popular
bullets.issue: 'tree-style' is vague; name the structure if you can, or drop the word.
bullets.suggestion: Precomputed a search index over popular workflows from a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table (Python/SQLAlchemy, Redis cache) to minimize DB queries under access limits

bullets.quote: Cut LLM workflow generation time 65% to under
Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline

bullets.issue: Lists AWS services without an outcome; low signal for HFT.
bullets.suggestion: Automated scheduled fine-tuning of a Bedrock source-relevancy model, gated to skip redundant retraining runs, with tracing and failure alerts

Co-founded a 110+ member campus product studio

structure.change: Order project bullets as correctness, latency/throughput, perf-variance debugging, storage benchmark, negative result.
structure.rationale: An HFT reviewer hires on hot-path latency and measurement discipline; those should come before the event-log storage work.

structure.change: Consider merging the B+ tree/LSM and batch-sizing bullets into one storage trade-off bullet.
structure.rationale: Frees a line and makes the C++ latency story stand out; both bullets cover the same off-hot-path subsystem.

structure.change: Keep Projects above Experience for this domain.
structure.rationale: The order book is the only HFT-relevant evidence; the experience section is cloud/LLM work.

top3: Move the latency/throughput bullet up to second and explain the mirror-book comparison in plain words; clarify whether 686.7 ns is a mean and add tail latency if you measured it
Simplify the batch-sizing bullet: lead with the conclusion (lookup-dominated, no query win), cut half the metrics, and say 'Documented' unless it was actually published
Tighten the storage benchmark bullet so the order book's correctness, latency, and perf-methodology story leads the page
